You are operating a real coding sandbox. Solve the task by interacting with the repository through the provided tools. 

Every response must be a tool call until the task is finished. Do not respond with ordinary assistant text, explanations, or code blocks. Text-only responses do not modify the repository and do not complete the task. 

Start by inspecting the repository and reading the relevant source file. After every tool call, carefully inspect the returned result before choosing the next action. The result may report success, failure, invalid arguments, a missing source match, test output, or another condition that requires a revised action. 

Make the smallest correct code change that solves the task. Prefer replace_lines when read_file provides clear line numbers. Use start_line and end_line exactly as shown by read_file, and replace only the smallest necessary range. For replace_lines, provide new_lines as a JSON array with exactly one source-code line per item. Do not write escaped newline sequences such as backslash-n inside an item. Preserve Python indentation exactly. When using edit_file, copy old_str exactly from the latest read_file output and include enough surrounding source text to make the match unique. Do not assume a modification succeeded without inspecting the tool result. 

If edit_file, replace_lines, or write_file fails, do not continue as if the repository was modified. Inspect the error, read the file again when necessary, revise the tool arguments, and retry the modification. You may call read_file, edit_file, replace_lines, and write_file multiple times. 

After a successful edit, line replacement, or file write, run tests. Inspect the test result carefully. If tests fail, revise the implementation and run tests again. You may repeat the inspect, modify, and test cycle until the repair is complete or the environment limit is reached. 

Call submit only after making a genuine repair attempt and running tests. The episode is complete only when submit succeeds. Do not stop with a text-only response before submitting.

Users on Windows keep reporting that the very first variable in their .env file is missing at runtime while every other variable loads fine. The cause is that some editors save the file with a leading byte-order mark. It is invisible, it is not whitespace, and nothing removes it, so it ends up glued to the front of the first key: the entry parses without error but under a name nobody will ever look up. When the first line uses an export prefix the file does not even parse cleanly. Fix the parser in dotenv/parser.py so a leading byte-order mark is discarded before parsing begins, including in the original text each binding records. Strip it only where it is meaningless - at the very start of the document. The same character appearing anywhere else is ordinary data and must be left alone.

tools.name: list_files
tools.description: List files in the sandbox, recursively. Start here to see the repo layout.

tools.name: read_file
tools.description: Read a file with line numbers. Returns at most 200 lines per call; use start/end to page through longer files.

start.description: Start of the public source window containing the parser entry function.

end.description: End of the public source window containing the parser entry function.

tools.name: write_file
tools.description: Write a whole file, replacing any existing content. Prefer edit_file for small changes.

content.description: The complete new contents of the file.

tools.name: edit_file
tools.description: Replace one exact snippet in a file. old_str must appear exactly once - include surrounding lines to make it unique.

old_str.description: Exact source text copied from the latest read_file output. Include surrounding lines when needed to make the match unique.

new_str.description: Replacement source text implementing the smallest correct repair.

tools.name: replace_lines
tools.description: Replace an inclusive range of 1-based source lines. Use line numbers from read_file. Replaces at most 12 existing lines per call.

start_line.description: First existing source line to replace, using the 1-based numbers from read_file.

end_line.description: Last existing source line to replace, inclusive.

new_lines.description: Replacement source code, one source line per array item. Copy indentation exactly. Use an empty array to delete the selected lines.

tools.name: run_tests
tools.description: Run the visible smoke tests. These are a sanity check, not the grading tests - passing them does not mean the task is solved.

tools.name: submit
tools.description: Finish the task. Call this once the fix is in place; the episode ends immediately.
